subject: Russia refinery attacks cross into systemwide domestic fuel deficit
body_md: Thesis: Ukraine's refinery-strike campaign has moved from isolated plant outages into measurable system-level Russian fuel impairment. Reuters reports late-August gasoline output around 80,000 t/day versus ~115,000 t/day summer demand (~70%), with imports and restrictions only lifting effective coverage to roughly 85%. This supersedes the narrower NORSI-outage state: the relevant graph is now refinery damage -> domestic production deficit -> imports/rationing/export controls -> logistics/inflation/war-economy pressure. Primary support: the Russian government imposed an Aug 1-Jan 31 fuel-export ban explicitly to stabilize the domestic fuel market. Independent observable corroboration includes widespread purchase limits and sharply reduced station availability reported before the latest outage wave. Contradiction: Russia retains crude abundance, import routes and repair capacity; deficits have previously eased, so do not promote this to strategic collapse. Alpha angle: refinery-by-refinery outage + rail/seaborne fuel imports + regional rationing + wholesale/retail spreads can become a leading physical-economy stress index.

signal.thesis: Sustained refinery attacks are now producing a systemwide Russian gasoline-supply deficit rather than only local outage headlines.
signal.what_would_falsify_this: Gasoline production recovers near or above domestic demand despite continued strikes; broad rationing/export restrictions unwind; or import/repair capacity closes the deficit without material price or availability stress.
